_comment: Routing-coverage ratchet seeds (road-to-routing-assurance 0.3). Coverage ratio = corpus cases / routed units, per scope, seeded at the MEASURED current value on 2026-08-25. CI fails only on a decrease -- the COUNT-ratchet disposition of lint_trigger_precision.ts. TWO scopes and never one aggregate: a blended figure would read ~0.46 and describe neither surface. Lowering a seed is a defect, not a fix: a ratio falls when a corpus case is removed OR when units are added without cases, and both are things to repair rather than to record.

measurement.rules: intersection of tests/eval/routing-matrix/*.yaml stems with the tier_1+tier_2 ids in dist/router.json, over that id count. Intersection rather than the file count, so a fixture naming no routed rule cannot raise the ratio.

seed_provenance.rules: 94 covered of 105 routed rules (tier-1 21/24, tier-2 73/81) on 2026-08-25.
seed_provenance.finding: The gap between the two seeds IS the roadmap defect D1, quantified. The rules surface is ~90% covered by a deterministic corpus that can fail a PR; the skills surface -- the one production routes on -- is 25%, covered only by a harness that is advisory only, never gating (rule_trigger_eval.ts:4).

history.reason: road-to-routing-assurance Phase 2.2 authored 14 high-tier corpus files (76 -> 90 of 299). The seed rises so the gain cannot be given back silently; it may never be LOWERED.
